transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Thursday, October 22. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'Badr MoU' won't put New Delhi-Jakarta missile contracts in jeopardy, experts say. Will 'Badr MoU' put India's recent defence agreements with Indonesia on advanced weaponry in jeopardy? Talking to TOI, Sudhir Kumar Mishra, DRDO chair (emeritus) and former director general, CEO and MD of BrahMos Aerospace, said, "Defence agreements with Indonesia have been done with enough safeguards and that only user manual, not technology of transfer manual, will be shared with Jakarta." French riots and Indian protests linked in same ecosystem: Report. Senior editor Asra Nomani's investigation says it has identified 101 organisations across nine countries in a "red-green protest ecosystem" (referring to Islamist and communist groups) that are coordinating, organising or amplifying protests in Europe in an expanding protest ecosystem. Her story also flags how transnational anti-capitalist organisation Progressive International (PI) explicitly grouped the current protests in France, Spain, India and Albania. One killed, 8 injured in Saudi airport attack amid US order for diplomats to leave. The United States ordered some of its diplomats and the family members of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia late on Wednesday. The move followed a series of deadly attacks attributed to Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels and growing concerns that the conflict could escalate further. The latest violence has raised concerns about the security of Saudi Arabia's critical infrastructure. Sexual offence charge rocks India's Asian Para Games contingent; swimmer faces ban. A senior PCI official, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nagoya and who handled the entire situation, confirmed the development to TOI, describing the alleged misconduct as "reprehensible and intolerable" and saying there could be "no justification" for such behaviour by an athlete representing the country on the international stage." Confidence in poll key for democracy, halt candidates' list: SC to Andhra poll body. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, said in 19 of the 100 urban local bodies , 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities/nagar panchayats , more than 63 percent of YSRCP candidates were prevented from filing nominations or their nomination papers were torn. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, for AP govt, said YSRCP was importing criminal elements from as far as Punjab and fomenting violence only to cry wolf later. Decades-old flaw discovered in PHP forces govt websites to go offline globally. Multiple government portals and public institutions experienced outages due to the revelation of PHP vulnerabilities. In an immediate response, IT teams mobilized to patch critical servers and thwart potential malicious attacks. Security analysts alerted that hackers swiftly targeted systems lacking updates. This vulnerability was unveiled through cutting-edge artificial intelligence tools that have transformed vulnerability detection. Missouri court overturns ruling giving couple ownership of neighbour's road. In a notable case from Missouri, a couple gained legal rights to their isolated property via their neighbor's land. Although the court initially granted them ownership of the access road, it later corrected this decision. Ultimately, they received a permanent easement, illustrating the difference between property rights and ownership. The couple can access their property while the neighbor retains the land under the road. At Jamnagar refinery, Rubio and Ambanis discuss energy, digital infrastructure. US President Donald Trump had earlier announced the setting up of a $300 billion refinery in US, with RIL being part of his plank to revive industry in the country and bring back jobs that were offshored. The Mukesh Ambani-led company has, however, not outlined any details. The importance of Reliance has since increased because the Jamnagar complex is where hard Venezuelan crude can be refined. Drug menace next target, says Amit Shah; eyes 2029 deadline. Stating that an environment conducive to development has emerged in Kashmir, Northeast and LWE-hit regions, Shah particularly thanked CRPF and its CoBRA battalion as well as Chhattisgarh Police for their role in the decisive fight against LWE. The home ministry will dedicate the remaining part of 2026 and three years after that to freeing the country from the drug menace, Shah said. SBI confirms data leak, says 4,000 customer records identified on dark web. The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 3,75,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses. Dolly Parton's former West Hollywood retreat listed for $12K monthly rent. Dolly Parton's former West Hollywood home has been taken off the rental market after being listed for $12,000 a month. The singer bought the two-bedroom property in 2007 for $1.2 million, later listing it for sale at $1.4 million in 2014. Records show the home changed hands in 2023 for $1.2 million.
